numerical_failure.observed_behavior: scipy.linalg.pinvh (Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of a Hermitian matrix) returns results that do not satisfy the Moore-Penrose conditions; for x = [[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]] the check np.allclose(y1 @ x @ y1, y1) is False, while the same checks with scipy.linalg.pinv are True. Cause: the eigh driver used internally (SYEVR, driver='evr') loses precision and returns a near-zero eigenvalue (2.66453526e-15 for the reported matrix) that is above the cutoff, whereas the true eigenvalue is 0; reported eigenvalues from eigvals/eigvalsh were 3, 1, and -3.36770206e-17 or 3.92505363e-17.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: pinvh should agree with scipy.linalg.pinv and satisfy the Moore-Penrose conditions; the analytically computed eigenvalues of the matrix are 3, 1, and 0, so the zero eigenvalue should be treated as zero. The fix changes pinvh to use driver='ev' (SYEV) in eigh.
trigger_conditions: Hermitian input matrix with a (near-)zero eigenvalue, e.g. x = [[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]]
pinvh uses eigh with the default SYEVR ('evr') driver, which can return a zero eigenvalue above the cutoff epsilon
default condition-number cutoff (atol/rtol not given); passing a very small rcond such as pinvh(a, rcond=1e-14) returned sensible results according to a maintainer comment
scipy version 1.4.1 with numpy 1.18.1 in the reported issue

input_output_examples.expected_output: True (same check holds for y2 = pinv(x), which returns True)

Issue #12515 notes eigh with driver='evr' returns eigenvalue 2.66453526e-15 while driver='ev' returns 9.99658224e-17 for the same matrix, indicating driver-dependent precision loss
PR and commit state SYEVR may sometimes give a zero eigenvalue greater than epsilon, and the fix switches pinvh to driver='ev' (SYEV), described as a bit more robust
The new test_zero_eigenvalue uses assert_allclose with atol=1e-15 checking Moore-Penrose conditions p@a@p ~ p and a@p@a ~ a
Issue reports np.allclose returns False for y1 @ x @ y1 ~ y1 while pinv results pass
Maintainer comment says pinvh(a, rcond=1e-14) gives sensible results, indicating the default cutoff is the trigger
Discussion says the fix should not be backported due to possible side effects
